It also overlaid a stress fracture of the two phalanxes.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Closed degloving injury of the foot (Morel-Lavallée lesion)
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old male sustained a crush injury to his foot from a motorcycle accident several weeks prior to presentation. He presented with pain on foot motion and swelling over the plantar surface. Initial X-ray at the time of injury showed no fracture. MRI and CT imaging on admission revealed two serous fluid collections characteristic of a closed degloving injury: a superficial collection (~48 cc) in the subcutaneous layer causing the plantar swelling, and a deeper collection (~38 cc) in the superficial fascial layer extending into the recesses of the fourth and fifth toe phalanxes, with an overlying stress fracture of these phalanxes. The vascular supply remained intact with no apparent nerve injury. The fluid collections were managed via incision and drainage with tissue debridement, followed by serial aseptic dressing changes. The patient was discharged when the dermis demonstrated signs of regeneration.
